title: myColorado app offline after state finds cybersecurity incident; data of 50,000 to 150,000 individuals may be affected
date_note: The Record says OIT discovered the incident on the evening of Nov. 18 and the Gazette says late the previous Wednesday; the state's own page is dated Nov. 23 and gives no earlier day.
org: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT)
geo_basis: state agency as the sources state it; the state capital is used for the pin
summary: Colorado's Governor's Office of Information Technology says it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving myColorado; KKTV and the Gazette report an unauthorized user accessed platform data. KKTV reports OIT estimated the data of between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals may be affected; the app has approximately 2.1 million users. The Gazette says affected users will be notified after the investigation; no restoration timeline has been given.
plain: Colorado's myColorado app is offline after the state found a cybersecurity incident. KKTV reports data of between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals may be affected, and the state gives no date for the app's return.
exec: A state digital-ID and services app is unavailable during the investigation, with data of between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals possibly affected, KKTV reports.
action: As the state's myColorado page advises, use your physical driver license or state-issued ID for identity verification and use agency websites for state services while the app is offline.

evidence.quote: OIT estimated that the cybersecurity incident may have impacted between 50,000 to 150,000 individuals' data.
The app has approximately 2.1 million users.

validation.note: State of Colorado's own myColorado page (primary) and KKTV both state the incident and that the app is offline; the 50,000 to 150,000 estimate and Nov. 18 discovery are from KKTV (9News page returned 403; Krystal 93 repeats the estimate). The state's page gives no figures. The Record and the Gazette (24 Nov) also report the incident, the Nov. 18 discovery, no restoration timeline and that affected users will be notified; the Gazette repeats the 50,000 to 150,000 estimate. The Record gives its own figure of nearly 150,000 and is not used for it.

review.note: Compared state page and KKTV: date, 50,000-150,000 and 2.1M figures, status, advice; front-page flag kept as the state notice has no specific URL
